Generation Details: Evol-Instruct is a data generation method that progressively evolves instruction prompts and their outputs to enhance the diversity and complexity of LLM training datasets. The TSEvol proposed in this work builds on Evol-Instruct by introducing a mechanism that dynamically incorporates time-series attributes at each evolution step. In each step, a subset of attributes is randomly selected from an attribute pool and added as additional context, guiding the LLMs to generate Q&A covering a broader range of time-series attributes according to the evolution type.

Generation Details: Specialized synthetic pipelines are used for different data subsets. The Align subset focuses on the model's time-series description ability (Cross-Modal Understanding), including 'ts2sem' and 'sem2ts,' where LLMs generate descriptions for specific time series and pair them with the series. The Match subset targets pattern recognition and matching ability (Sequence Matching), divided into Isomorphic (find similar sequence), Robust (find smoothed sequence), Localization (find similar sequence in longer sequences), and Reverse (find reversed sequence), each constructed using template-based prompts. Base questions are generated from 17 manually curated templates covering trend, volatility, seasonality, noise, stationarity, and local-global attributes. The InWild dataset uses a three-stage synthetic pipeline: LLM description generation, LLM dynamic question-answer-explanation generation, and human-LLM verification.
